summary: The note describes a town's grassroots pollution-reduction movement led by Clean Air for All (CAFA) and founder Maria Thompson, centered on the "Cycle for Change" campaign launched in September 2023. It covers cycling workshops, new bike lanes, the "Bikes in Business" program, the "Green Lung" planting project, school "Bike and Learn" sessions, and the Clean Air Carnival. Environmental Monitoring Committee data from September 1st shows a downward trend in air pollution, and Mayor Andrew Jacobs praised the movement as a model.
one_line: A town's cycling, greening and education campaigns led by Clean Air for All have produced a measurable decline in air pollution.
key_facts: Maria Thompson, founder of the non-profit Clean Air for All (CAFA), launched the "Cycle for Change" initiative in September 2023 to encourage residents to swap cars for bikes.
Thompson gave an interview on October 6th saying cycling cuts emissions while also providing exercise and a better quality of life.
CAFA began free cycling workshops in early November for both novice and seasoned riders.
As of December 15th, new bike lanes began to intertwine with city roads to make cycling safer.
"Bikes in Business" launched January 10th; David Henderson, owner of Henderson's Cafe, offers discounts to customers who show a bike helmet.
Cycle delivery services replaced some van runs, leading to a significant drop in local traffic congestion as reported in early February.
Botanist Laura Sanchez led the "Green Lung" project, unveiled March 20th, to increase urban green spaces that absorb pollution.
The town's newest park, "Oxygen Oasis," features plant species known for air-purifying qualities.
Starting April 5th, local schools began weekly 'Bike and Learn' sessions teaching sustainability, pollution science and safe cycling.
The Clean Air Carnival was held on August 25th with a parade of bicycles, unicycles and tricycles, followed by a fair at Oxygen Oasis powered partly by stationary bike generators.
The town's Environmental Monitoring Committee released data on September 1st showing a downward trend in air pollution levels.
Mayor Andrew Jacobs said the community's vitality is measured by the quality of the air shared, not the cars driven, and called the movement a model for others.
